title: The 2019 Notre-Dame fire and the debate over rebuilding its spire

sources.title: A restored Notre Dame cathedral is unveiled days before its official reopening (2024-11-29)
Architecture Competition To Rebuild Notre Dame's Spire Is Announced (2019-04-18)

After months of debate over its design, the rebuilt Notre Dame will look … exactly the same (2020-07-09)

facts.text: On April 15, 2019, a fire broke out in the roof framework of Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, and its 19th-century spire collapsed.

Days after the fire, French Prime Minister Edouard Philippe announced an international architecture competition to decide whether the spire should be rebuilt identically in wood and lead or adapted to the present day.
President Emmanuel Macron said he wanted the cathedral rebuilt within five years.
The spire that collapsed had been designed by architect Eugene Viollet-le-Duc and built in 1859, after a 20-year restoration of the cathedral.
When Viollet-le-Duc's spire was new it was controversial, but over time it came to represent Paris and France.
Architects proposed bold designs after the fire, including a glass design with solar power and an urban farm, and a greenhouse roof with a spire filled with beehives.
Macron had supported a contemporary design, but in July 2020 he backed restoring the spire exactly as it had been, ending the debate over new designs.
The new spire was built by carpenters from oak, as an exact replica of Viollet-le-Duc's design.
Notre-Dame reopened with ceremonies beginning on December 7, 2024.
The restored cathedral is more than 800 years old.
Derived: Viollet-le-Duc's spire stood from 1859 until the 2019 fire, about 160 years; the cathedral reopened more than five years after the fire.
